title: Generic min_max and dedup
prompt:
Practice generics and trait bounds.

1. min_max<T: PartialOrd + Copy>(xs: &[T]) -> Option<(T, T)> returns the smallest and largest element in a single pass, or None for an empty slice. If there are ties, any equal element is fine.

2. dedup_consecutive<T: PartialEq + Clone>(xs: &[T]) -> Vec<T> returns a new Vec with consecutive duplicate elements collapsed into one (like the Unix uniq command). Do not use Vec::dedup.

Both functions must work for any type meeting the bounds, e.g. i32, f64, char, &str.

Example:
  min_max(&[3, 9, -2, 7]) -> Some((-2, 9))
  dedup_consecutive(&[1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 1, 3, 3]) -> [1, 2, 1, 3]
